---
title: "Canvas, Quizzes, and Quarto"
---

Quarto should not replace Canvas. Canvas remains the official teaching system for enrolments, announcements, assignments, quizzes, deadlines, and the gradebook.

Quarto handles the materials that Canvas handles poorly: long-form notes, code examples, templates, weekly pages, book chapters, and public-facing course resources.

## Recommended division of labour

| Need | Use Canvas | Use Quarto |
|---|---|---|
| Announcements | yes | no |
| Official due dates | yes | optional mirror |
| Gradebook | yes | no |
| Graded quizzes | yes | no |
| Assignment submission | yes | no |
| Weekly lecture notes | link out | yes |
| Code examples | link out | yes |
| Templates | link out | yes |
| Public course website | no | yes |
| Book/exportable text | no | yes |

## Quarto and quizzes

Quarto is not a quiz engine and does not provide a Canvas-style gradebook. Use Canvas New Quizzes or the institutional LMS for all graded quizzes.

Quarto can still host:

- practice questions,
- worked examples,
- quiz study guides,
- links to Canvas quizzes,
- ungraded self-check questions,
- embedded H5P or external quiz widgets if the institution supports them.

## Weekly Canvas shell

A simple Canvas weekly module can be:

```text
Week 4 — Interactive Data Apps with Streamlit
1. Read the Quarto Week 4 page
2. Download the starter app template
3. Complete Canvas Quiz 4
4. Submit the Streamlit MVP checkpoint
```

## Why keep quizzes in Canvas?

Canvas handles authentication, timing, accessibility accommodations, submissions, grades, and institutional records. Quarto is better treated as the publishing layer, not the assessment-management layer.
